**Answer**

The latest stable Bun release I found as of **August 27, 2026** is **Bun v1.4.0** (marketed as **Bun 1.4**). The official GitHub release page marks **Bun v1.4** as **“Latest”**, and the official Bun blog lists **“Bun 1.4”** as the latest release and shows **“Install Bun v1.4.0.”**  
Sources: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.0 , https://bun.com/blog

It was published on **August 20, 2026** according to the dated official release post for Bun 1.4.  
Source: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

**Most consequential changes, according to the official release sources**

`Supported fact:` Bun 1.4 is the first Bun release written in Rust; the release post says, “Bun is now written in Rust.”  
Source: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

`Supported fact:` The release post highlights a major **Node.js compatibility** jump: Bun 1.4 adds **1,517 newly passing tests** from the **Node.js v26.3.0** test suite, which the post calls Bun’s biggest compatibility jump since 1.0.  
Source: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

`Supported fact:` The release post also foregrounds large **runtime/performance** changes: **5x lower idle CPU usage**, **up to 35% lower memory usage**, and **50% faster startup on Linux**.  
Source: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

`Supported fact:` Bun 1.4 adds several major built-ins that replace common external tools, including **`Bun.Image`** for image processing, **`Bun.WebView`** for headless browser automation, **`Bun.markdown`** for Markdown parsing/rendering, **`Bun.cron()`** for scheduling, and **`Bun.Terminal`** for pseudo-terminal control.  
Sources: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4 , https://bun.com/blog

`Supported fact:` Bun 1.4 adds **parallel script execution** via **`bun run --parallel`**, **parallel test execution** via **`bun test --parallel`**, and package-management commands such as **`bun audit fix`**, **`bun dedupe`**, and **`bun prune`**.  
Source: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

`Supported fact:` Bun 1.4 introduces an opt-in **global virtual store** for isolated installs; the release post says this can deliver **up to 7x faster installs**.  
Sources: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4 , https://bun.com/blog

**Inference**

`Inference:` If “most consequential” means “most emphasized by Bun’s own official release materials,” the top changes are probably: **the Rust rewrite**, **the large Node.js compatibility jump**, **the runtime/performance improvements**, and **the new built-in standard-library features/tools**. I infer that from the blog homepage summary and the Bun 1.4 release post’s lead section and section prominence, not from an explicit ranked list.  
Sources used for the inference: https://bun.com/blog , https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

**Disagreement, uncertainty, and evidence quality**

`Disagreement:` I found **no disagreement** between the official Bun blog and the official GitHub release page about the latest stable release being Bun 1.4 / v1.4.0.  
Sources: https://bun.com/blog , https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.0

`Uncertainty:` The GitHub page I opened shows the release time as **“20 Aug 14:07”** in relative UI formatting, while the Bun blog gives the explicit calendar date **August 20, 2026**. The year is explicit on the blog post, so I rely on the blog for the full publication date.  
Sources: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.0 , https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

`Lack of good evidence:` I did **not** find an official Bun source that explicitly ranks changes by importance, so any ordering of “most consequential” changes is necessarily an inference from Bun’s own summaries and headings rather than a directly stated official ranking.  
Sources: https://bun.com/blog , https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4
